SelectableIcon¶

class urwid.SelectableIcon(text: _TagMarkup, cursor_position: int | None = 0, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.LEFT, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = WrapMode.SPACE, layout: TextLayout | None = None)¶

Selectable text widget that shows a fixed-position cursor when focused.

Create a text widget that is selectable.

A cursor is displayed at a fixed location in the text when in focus, unless cursor_position is None. This widget has no special handling of keyboard or mouse input.

Parameters:

  • text – markup for this widget; see Text for description of text markup

  • cursor_position – position the cursor will appear in the text when this widget is in focus; None shows no cursor

  • align – typically 'left', 'center' or 'right'

  • wrap – typically 'space', 'any', 'clip' or 'ellipsis'

  • layout – defaults to a shared StandardTextLayout instance

Return the position of the cursor if visible.

This method is required for widgets that display a cursor.

No keys are handled by this widget.

This method is required for selectable widgets.

render(size: tuple[int] | tuple[()], focus: bool = False) → TextCanvas | CompositeCanvas¶

Render the text content of this widget with a cursor when in focus.

>>> si = SelectableIcon("[!]")
>>> si
<SelectableIcon selectable fixed/flow widget '[!]'>
>>> si.render((4,), focus=True).cursor
(0, 0)
>>> si = SelectableIcon("((*))", 2)
>>> si.render((8,), focus=True).cursor
(2, 0)
>>> si.render((2,), focus=True).cursor
(0, 1)
>>> si.render(()).cursor
>>> si.render(()).text
[b'((*))']
>>> si.render((), focus=True).cursor
(2, 0)
>>> SelectableIcon("item", None).render((8,), focus=True).cursor

ANSIText¶

class urwid.ANSIText(ansi_text: str, previous_attr: AttrSpec | ParsedLine | ANSIText | None = None, *, one_line: bool = False, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = WrapMode.SPACE, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.LEFT)¶

A read-only widget interpreting ANSI/VT100 colour, horizontal and (optionally) vertical movement escapes.

It acts almost exactly like a read-only Text widget for the resolved, escape-free content.

Parsing is delegated to urwid.ansi_parser.AnsiParser, and layout (wrapping, alignment, packing and rendering) is delegated to an internal Text instance that this widget wraps via WidgetWrap, so this widget’s pack/render/rows behaviour is identical to Text for the same resolved characters, without needing to forward those calls by hand.

By default (one_line=False), a newline genuinely starts a new row, CSI n A/B genuinely moves the cursor up/down between rows, and a bare \r genuinely overwrites the current row in place (letting progress-bar-style redraw sequences resolve correctly) – ansi_text is treated as a single, complete block, meant to render one already-complete captured screen/block.

Pass one_line=True to restrict this widget to a single physical line of resolved text; see AnsiParser’s one_line flag for the underlying parsing semantics. In this mode, line ends and vertical cursor movement are treated as meaningless outside a single line (stripped/split rather than resolved into rows): since the underlying parser always returns a tuple[ParsedLine, ...] in this mode (line ends, VT and FF outside an OSC string are structural split points, never silently discarded), constructing an ANSIText directly from text containing an embedded line end only surfaces the first resulting line – no data is lost (the full split is always computed), but only the first line is exposed by this widget instance. Use from_lines() to turn arbitrary multi-line (or arbitrarily chunked) raw text into a complete sequence of ANSIText instances, in either mode.

>>> ANSIText("hello")
<ANSIText fixed/flow widget 'hello'>
>>> ANSIText("a\nb").text
'a\nb'
>>> ANSIText("a\nb", one_line=True).text
'a'

Build the widget from a block of ANSI/VT100-escaped text.

Parameters:

  • ansi_text – a block of text, optionally spanning several lines and containing ANSI/VT100 escape sequences. If one_line is true, only its first physical line is surfaced by this widget instance.

  • previous_attr – SGR/colour state to carry in from previously parsed text (see last_attr), or the ANSIText or ParsedLine of that text, to carry its character sets in as well.

  • one_line – restrict this widget to a single physical line of resolved text rather than resolving the whole block into multi-row output.

  • wrap – forwarded to the internal Text.

  • align – forwarded to the internal Text.

property attrib: list[tuple[Hashable, int]]¶

Read-only property returning the run-length encoded display attributes of this widget’s text.

property bel: int¶

The number of BEL characters seen (aggregated over the whole block unless one_line is true).

classmethod from_lines(chunks: Iterable[str], previous_attr: AttrSpec | ParsedLine | ANSIText | None = None, *, one_line: bool = False, **kwargs: Any) → Iterator[ANSIText]¶

Consume raw ANSI text chunks and yield the resulting ANSIText widget(s).

chunks (e.g. successive os.read() results from a subprocess) are not required to be pre-split on line boundaries, and each chunk may contain zero, one, or several line ends. Internally accumulates a single AnsiParser across all chunks, so a line split across two chunk boundaries – or an escape sequence split across two chunk boundaries – is still resolved correctly, and calls finalize() only once the iterable is exhausted.

If one_line is true, one ANSIText is yielded per line the shared parser completes, in order, with SGR colour state and character sets carried forward continuously: each produced ANSIText continues from the previous one, whether that previous line came from the same chunk or an earlier one.

If one_line is false (the default), this naturally reduces to yielding exactly one ANSIText once every chunk has been consumed, representing the entire accumulated multi-chunk block resolved into real multi-row output – the “normal multiline” case, reached through the same code path as the one_line=True case rather than a separate one.

Parameters:

  • chunks – an iterable of raw text chunks, not required to be aligned on line or escape-sequence boundaries.

  • previous_attr – SGR/colour state to seed the shared parser with, as if it were carried over from previously parsed text, or the ANSIText or ParsedLine of that text, to carry its character sets in as well.

  • one_line – parse in single-line-splitting mode (see the class docstring) rather than resolving the whole accumulated input into one multi-row block.

  • kwargs – forwarded to _from_parsed() (i.e. wrap/align for the internal Text).

Yields:

one or more ANSIText instances, in order, depending on one_line.

get_text() → tuple[str | bytes, list[tuple[Hashable, int]]]¶

Return (text, display attributes), see urwid.Text.get_text().

property last_attr: AttrSpec | None¶

The SGR/colour state in effect at the very end of this widget’s text.

Feed this in as previous_attr to a subsequently constructed ANSIText to continue the same colour state; feed this widget itself instead to continue the character sets (such as the DEC Special Graphics line drawing) as well.

property leds: str | None¶

The last keyboard-LED state requested, if any.

set_ansi_text(ansi_text: str, previous_attr: AttrSpec | ParsedLine | ANSIText | None = None) → None¶

Re-parse ansi_text and invalidate this widget.

Parsing uses the mode (one_line) this widget was constructed with; if one_line is true, only the first resulting line is used, see the class docstring.

Parameters:

  • ansi_text – a block of text, optionally spanning several lines and containing ANSI/VT100 escape sequences.

  • previous_attr – SGR/colour state to carry in from previously parsed text (see last_attr), or the ANSIText or ParsedLine of that text, to carry its character sets in as well.

property text: str | bytes¶

Read-only property returning the resolved, escape-free text of this widget (may contain \n).

property title: str | None¶

The last OSC window-title string seen, if any.

Decoration Widget Classes¶

AttrMap¶

class urwid.AttrMap(w: WrappedWidget, attr_map: _AttrMapLike, focus_map: _AttrMapLike = None)¶

A decoration that maps one set of display attributes to another.

This object will pass all function calls and variable references to the wrapped widget.

Parameters:

  • w – widget to wrap (stored as self.original_widget)

  • attr_map – attribute to apply to w, or dict of old display attribute: new display attribute mappings; the other attributes of w are placed over the attribute of None, so their ‘inherit’ colors are taken from it (see LayeredAttr), and an attribute mapped to None shows the attribute of None

  • focus_map – attribute to apply when in focus or dict of old display attribute: new display attribute mappings; if None use attr

>>> from urwid import Divider, Edit, Text
>>> AttrMap(Divider("!"), "bright")
<AttrMap flow widget <Divider flow widget '!'> attr_map={None: 'bright'}>
>>> AttrMap(Edit(), "notfocus", "focus").attr_map
{None: 'notfocus'}
>>> AttrMap(Edit(), "notfocus", "focus").focus_map
{None: 'focus'}
>>> size = (5,)
>>> am = AttrMap(Text("hi"), "greeting", "fgreet")
>>> next(am.render(size, focus=False).content())  # ... = b in Python 3
[('greeting', None, ...'hi   ')]
>>> next(am.render(size, focus=True).content())
[('fgreet', None, ...'hi   ')]
>>> am2 = AttrMap(Text(("word", "hi")), {"word": "greeting", None: "bg"})
>>> am2
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={'word': 'greeting', None: 'bg'}>
>>> next(am2.render(size).content())
[(LayeredAttr('greeting', 'bg'), None, ...'hi'), ('bg', None, ...'   ')]
property attr_map: dict[Hashable, Hashable]¶

Return a copy of the attribute mapping dictionary.

property focus_map: dict[Hashable, Hashable] | None¶

Return a copy of the focus attribute mapping dictionary, or None if unset.

get_attr_map() → dict[Hashable, Hashable]¶

Return a copy of the attribute mapping dictionary.

get_focus_map() → dict[Hashable, Hashable] | None¶

Return a copy of the focus attribute mapping dictionary, or None if unset.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render wrapped widget and apply attribute. Return canvas.

set_attr_map(attr_map: _AttrMapLike) → None¶

Set the attribute mapping dictionary {from_attr: to_attr, …}.

A single attribute is stored as {None: attribute}, the way the constructor does.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> w = AttrMap(Text("hi"), None)
>>> w.set_attr_map({"a": "b"})
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={'a': 'b'}>
>>> w.set_attr_map("c")
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={None: 'c'}>
Raises:

AttrMapError – a key or value of the mapping is not hashable.

set_focus_map(focus_map: _AttrMapLike | None) → None¶

Set the focus attribute mapping dictionary {from_attr: to_attr, …}.

If None this widget will use the attr mapping instead (no change when in focus).

A single attribute is stored as {None: attribute}, the way the constructor does.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> w = AttrMap(Text("hi"), {})
>>> w.set_focus_map({"a": "b"})
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={} focus_map={'a': 'b'}>
>>> w.set_focus_map("c")
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={} focus_map={None: 'c'}>
>>> w.set_focus_map(None)
>>> w
<AttrMap fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget 'hi'> attr_map={}>
Raises:

AttrMapError – a key or value of the mapping is not hashable.

Padding¶

class urwid.Padding(w: WrappedWidget, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE, 'fixed left', 'fixed right'], int] = Align.LEFT, width: int | Literal['pack', 'clip', WHSettings.PACK, WHSettings.CLIP] | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE, 'fixed left', 'fixed right'], int] | None = (WHSettings.RELATIVE, 100), min_width: int | None = None, left: int = 0, right: int = 0)¶

Decoration that adds blank columns to the left and/or right of a wrapped widget.

Build the widget, padding w on the left and/or right.

Parameters:

  • w – a box, flow or fixed widget to pad on the left and/or right this widget is stored as self.original_widget

  • align – one of: 'left', 'center', 'right' ('relative', percentage 0=left 100=right)

  • width –

    one of:

    given width

    integer number of columns for self.original_widget

    'pack'

    try to pack self.original_widget to its ideal size

    ('relative', percentage of total width)

    make width depend on the container’s width

    'clip'

    to enable clipping mode for a fixed widget

  • min_width – the minimum number of columns for self.original_widget or None

  • left – a fixed number of columns to pad on the left

  • right – a fixed number of columns to pad on the right

Clipping Mode: (width= 'clip') In clipping mode this padding widget will behave as a flow widget and self.original_widget will be treated as a fixed widget. self.original_widget will be clipped to fit the available number of columns. For example if align is 'left' then self.original_widget may be clipped on the right.

Pack Mode: (width= 'pack') In pack mode is supported FIXED operation if it is supported by the original widget.

>>> from urwid import Divider, Text, BigText, FontRegistry
>>> from urwid.util import set_temporary_encoding
>>> size = (7,)
>>> def pr(w):
...     with set_temporary_encoding("utf-8"):
...         for t in w.render(size).text:
...             print(f"|{t.decode('utf-8')}|")
>>> pr(Padding(Text("Head"), ("relative", 20), "pack"))
| Head  |
>>> pr(Padding(Divider("-"), left=2, right=1))
|  ---- |
>>> pr(Padding(Divider("*"), "center", 3))
|  ***  |
>>> p = Padding(Text("1234"), "left", 2, None, 1, 1)
>>> p
<Padding fixed/flow widget <Text fixed/flow widget '1234'> left=1 right=1 width=2>
>>> pr(p)  # align against left
| 12    |
| 34    |
>>> p.align = "right"
>>> pr(p)  # align against right
|    12 |
|    34 |
>>> pr(Padding(Text("hi\nthere"), "right", "pack"))  # pack text first
|  hi   |
|  there|
>>> pr(Padding(BigText("1,2,3", FontRegistry["Thin 3x3"]()), width="clip"))
| ┐  ┌─┐|
| │  ┌─┘|
| ┴ ,└─ |
property align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]¶

Return the padding alignment setting.

Number of columns of padding on the left.

Minimum width of the wrapped widget, or None for no minimum.

move_cursor_to_coords(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], x: int | Literal['left', 'right', Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT], y: int) → bool¶

Returns:

True if move succeeded, False otherwise.

pack(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int] = (), focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the size the widget would render as, for FIXED sizing.

A GIVEN width over a FIXED widget that is not FLOW takes the given width and the wrapped widget’s rows.

Raises:

PaddingError – this Padding uses CLIP, which makes it FLOW-only. Its width type does not resolve to a fixed size. Its width is GIVEN and the wrapped widget supports neither FLOW nor FIXED and has no rows(). This error is an AttributeError as well.

Warns PaddingWarning:

the wrapped widget does not support the sizing a FIXED pack needs: FLOW or FIXED for a GIVEN width, FIXED otherwise.

padding_values(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the number of columns to pad on the left and right.

Override this method to define custom padding behaviour.

Raises:

PaddingError – this Padding uses CLIP and no size was given.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas¶

Render the Padding and return the resulting canvas.

Raises:

ValueError – the Padding is empty and no size was given.

Warns PaddingWarning:

the width is GIVEN and size is too narrow for it.

right¶

Number of columns of padding on the right.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the rows needed for self.original_widget.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Widget sizing.

Rules: * width == CLIP: only FLOW is supported, and wrapped widget should support FIXED * width == GIVEN: FIXED is supported when the wrapped widget supports FLOW or FIXED * All other cases: use sizing of target widget

Warns PaddingWarning:

the width is GIVEN and the wrapped widget supports none of FLOW, BOX and FIXED sizing.

property width: Literal[WHSettings.CLIP, WHSettings.PACK] | int | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]¶

Return the padding width.

Filler¶

class urwid.Filler(body: WrappedWidget, valign: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom'] | VAlign | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] = VAlign.MIDDLE, height: int | Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK] | tuple[Literal['relative', 'fixed top', 'fixed bottom', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int] | None = WHSettings.PACK, min_height: int | None = None, top: int = 0, bottom: int = 0, *, shrink_to_fit: bool = False)¶

Box widget decoration that vertically aligns a flow or box widget within the available space.

Parameters:

  • body – a flow widget or box widget to be filled around (stored as self.original_widget)

  • valign – one of: 'top', 'middle', 'bottom', ('relative', percentage 0=top 100=bottom)

  • height –

    one of:

    'pack'

    if body is a flow widget

    given height

    integer number of rows for self.original_widget

    ('relative', percentage of total height)

    make height depend on container’s height

  • min_height –

    one of:

    None

    if no minimum or if body is a flow widget

    minimum height

    integer number of rows for the widget when height not fixed

  • top – a fixed number of rows to fill at the top

  • bottom – a fixed number of rows to fill at the bottom

  • shrink_to_fit – with a 'pack' height, render a body taller than the rows available as a box at those rows, instead of clipping it. It applies only to a body that also supports 'box', such as a LineBox around a Table. It has no effect for other heights.

Raises:

FillerError – valign is not a vertical alignment value, or a fixed height is combined with a valign it cannot be used with.

If body is a flow widget, then height must be 'pack' and min_height will be ignored. Sizing of the filler will be BOX/FLOW in this case.

If height is integer, min_height will be ignored and sizing of filler will be BOX/FLOW.

Filler widgets will try to satisfy height argument first by reducing the valign amount when necessary. If height still cannot be satisfied it will also be reduced.

bottom¶

Number of blank rows below the body.

filler_values(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], focus: bool) → tuple[int, int]¶

Return the number of rows to pad on the top and bottom.

Override this method to define custom padding behaviour.

With shrink_to_fit, a 'pack' height taller than the rows available is cut down to those rows.

LineBox¶

class urwid.LineBox(original_widget: WrappedWidget, title: _TagMarkup = '', title_align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.CENTER, title_attr: Hashable = None, tlcorner: str = '┌', tline: str = '─', lline: str = '│', trcorner: str = '┐', blcorner: str = '└', rline: str = '│', bline: str = '─', brcorner: str = '┘')¶

Box widget decoration that draws a line border, with an optional title, around another widget.

Draw a line around original_widget.

Use ‘title’ to set an initial title text with will be centered on top of the box. It may be any text markup accepted by Text. A title wider than the top line is cut with an ellipsis.

Use title_attr to apply a specific attribute to the title text.

Use title_align to align the title to the ‘left’, ‘right’, or ‘center’. The default is ‘center’.

You can also override the widgets used for the lines/corners:

tline: top line bline: bottom line lline: left line rline: right line tlcorner: top left corner trcorner: top right corner blcorner: bottom left corner brcorner: bottom right corner

If empty string is specified for one of the lines/corners, then no character will be output there. If no top/bottom/left/right lines - whole lines will be omitted. This allows for seamless use of adjoining LineBoxes.

Class attribute Symbols can be used as source for standard lines:

>>> print(LineBox(Text("Some text")).render(()))
┌─────────┐
│Some text│
└─────────┘
>>> print(
...     LineBox(
...         Text("Some text"),
...         tlcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.TOP_LEFT_ROUNDED,
...         trcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.TOP_RIGHT_ROUNDED,
...         blcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.BOTTOM_LEFT_ROUNDED,
...         brcorner=LineBox.Symbols.LIGHT.BOTTOM_RIGHT_ROUNDED,
...     ).render(())
... )
╭─────────╮
│Some text│
╰─────────╯
>>> print(
...     LineBox(
...         Text("Some text"),
...         tline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.HORIZONTAL,
...         bline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.HORIZONTAL,
...         lline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.VERTICAL,
...         rline=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.VERTICAL,
...         tlcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.TOP_LEFT,
...         trcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.TOP_RIGHT,
...         blcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.BOTTOM_LEFT,
...         brcorner=LineBox.Symbols.HEAVY.BOTTOM_RIGHT,
...     ).render(())
... )
┏━━━━━━━━━┓
┃Some text┃
┗━━━━━━━━━┛

To make Table constructions, some lineboxes need to be drawn without sides and T or CROSS symbols used for corners of cells.

Raises:

ValueError – a title with text is given while tline is empty, or title_align is not a supported alignment.

property focus: AbstractWidget | None¶

LineBox is partially container.

While focus position is a bit hacky (formally it’s not container and only position 0 available), focus widget is always provided by original widget.

format_title(text: _TagMarkup) → _TagMarkup¶

Return text padded with spaces for display in the box’s top border, or an empty string if unset.

A string stays a string; other text markup is returned as the list [" ", text, " "]. Markup with no text, such as ("attr", ""), counts as unset.

property original_widget: WrappedWidget¶

Return the widget wrapped by the line box.

set_title(text: _TagMarkup) → None¶

Set the title shown in the top line of the box.

Raises:

ValueError – this LineBox has no top line to put a title on.

Pop-up Widget Classes¶

PopUpLauncher¶

class urwid.PopUpLauncher(original_widget: LauncherWidget, *, close_on_menu: bool = False, close_on_click_outside: bool = False)¶

Decoration that lets a wrapped widget open and close a pop-up drawn over other widgets by a PopUpTarget.

Wrap original_widget, with no pop-up open yet.

Parameters:

  • original_widget – widget that opens the pop-up.

  • close_on_menu – close the pop-up when it leaves a key for the menu command (esc by default) unhandled while it is the topmost open pop-up.

  • close_on_click_outside – close the pop-up on a press of mouse button 1, 2 or 3 outside it while it is the topmost open pop-up. The press closes the pop-up only, and does not reach the widget under it.

close_pop_up() → None¶

Discard the currently open pop-up widget, if any, and invalidate this widget.

create_pop_up() → AbstractWidget¶

Return the widget to be used for the pop-up.

Subclass must override this method. It is called once each time the pop-up is opened.

PopUpTarget renders the pop-up with the box size declared by get_pop_up_parameters(), so the widget returned here must accept an (overlay_width, overlay_height) size. Wrap a flow or fixed widget in a Filler (or in another box container) before returning it.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – the subclass does not override this method.

get_pop_up_parameters() → PopUpParametersModel¶

Return a dict of pop-up parameters.

For example: {'left': 0, 'top': 1, 'overlay_width': 30, 'overlay_height': 4, 'anchor_height': 1}.

Subclass must override this method. It is called each time this widget is rendered.

The optional anchor_height key makes PopUpTarget move the pop-up above the launcher, or clip its height, when it does not fit below; see CompositeCanvas.set_pop_up.

Raises:

NotImplementedError – the subclass does not override this method.

property launcher_size: tuple[int, int] | None¶

The (columns, rows) of the last render that was not served from the canvas cache, or None before it.

It is set before get_pop_up_parameters() is called, so inside that method it is always the size being rendered.

open_pop_up() → None¶

Create the pop-up widget via create_pop_up() and invalidate this widget.

property pop_up_widget: AbstractWidget | None¶

The open pop-up widget, or None when the pop-up is closed.

render(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas | Canvas¶

Render the wrapped widget, attaching the open pop-up widget to the canvas, if any.

PopUpTarget¶

class urwid.PopUpTarget(original_widget: WrappedWidget)¶

Box widget that overlays the pop-up(s) declared by a PopUpLauncher inside it.

Pop-ups nest: a pop-up widget may itself be a PopUpLauncher with its own pop-up open, in which case it is drawn overlaid on top of the pop-up that opened it, and so on for as many levels as are open at once.

Wrap original_widget, which is rendered with any open pop-up(s) overlaid on top.

Parameters:

original_widget – box widget to wrap; typically contains a PopUpLauncher.

enter_selectable(*, reverse: bool = False) → None¶

Do nothing: every focus under this widget is kept when a parent container enters it.

The widget that receives keys is known only after the pop-ups were laid out at the current size, which the entry hook does not have, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[int, int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return the cursor coordinates of the current widget.

Raises:

TypeError – the current widget has no get_cursor_coords method.

get_pref_col(size: tuple[int, int]) → int | Literal['left', 'right', Align.LEFT, Align.RIGHT] | None¶

Return the preferred cursor column of the current widget, or None if it has none.

Raises:

TypeError – the current widget has no get_pref_col method.

keypress(size: tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and forward the keypress to it.

A key the topmost pop-up leaves unhandled goes to the on_unhandled_key callback its launcher set, if any; see CompositeCanvas.set_pop_up.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and forward the mouse event to it.

A press of mouse button 1, 2 or 3 outside the topmost pop-up goes to the on_click_outside callback its launcher set, if any. The press is then handled and does not reach the widgets under the pop-up. See CompositeCanvas.set_pop_up.

move_cursor_to_coords(size: tuple[int, int], x: int, y: int) → bool¶

Move the cursor of the current widget to (x, y).

Raises:

TypeError – the current widget has no move_cursor_to_coords method.

pack(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[()] = (), focus: bool = False) → tuple[int, int]¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and return the current widget’s packed size.

render(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → Canvas¶

Rebuild the pop-up overlay chain for size and render the resulting widget.

Special Widget Classes¶

Notifications¶

class urwid.Notifications(*, timeout: float | None = 5.0, max_count: int | None = None, severity_attr: Mapping[Severity, _AttrMapLike] | None = None, default: _TagMarkup | None = None, default_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, loop: MainLoop | None = None, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align = Align.LEFT, wrap: Literal['space', 'any', 'clip', 'ellipsis'] | WrapMode = WrapMode.SPACE)¶

A flow widget listing messages, each shown until its timeout runs out or it is dismissed.

The oldest message is at the top. With max_count set, a new message dismisses the oldest ones over that count, so max_count=1 makes a status line. While no message is showing, the default text is shown, or nothing, in zero rows.

A message with a timeout sets an alarm on loop, or, without one, on the MainLoop running when notify() is called (see get_running_loop()). The loop redraws the screen after the alarm, so an expired message disappears with no further call.

Sends "change" once per notify(), dismiss(), clear(), expiry, or lowered max_count that changed the messages shown, once the change is complete. Its handlers receive the widget. An exception raised by a handler during an expiry is logged by the loop, as for every alarm callback.

Important

Call every method from the thread running the loop, like every other widget change. Another thread hands the message over with MainLoop.call_from_thread() instead.

>>> status = Notifications(max_count=1, default="ready")
>>> status.render((8,)).text
[b'ready   ']
>>> saved = status.notify("saved", timeout=None)
>>> status.render((8,)).text
[b'saved   ']
>>> status.dismiss(saved)
True
>>> status.render((8,)).text
[b'ready   ']

Build an empty notification list.

Parameters:

  • timeout – seconds a message stays when notify() is not given one, see timeout.

  • max_count – messages shown at once, see max_count.

  • severity_attr – attribute map applied to a message for each Severity, see severity_attr.

  • default – text markup shown while no message is showing, or None to show nothing.

  • default_attr – attribute map applied to the default text, in any form AttrMap takes.

  • loop – loop the alarms are set on. None uses the loop running at each notify().

  • align – alignment of the text of every message and of the default text.

  • wrap – wrap mode of the text of every message and of the default text.

Raises:

  • TypeError – timeout is not a number or None, max_count is not an int or None, or a key of severity_attr is not a Severity.

  • ValueError – timeout is not finite and > 0, or max_count is < 1.

  • TextError – align or wrap is not supported by the text layout.

  • TagMarkupException – default is not valid text markup.

  • AttrMapError – a key or value of an attribute map is not hashable.

clear() → None¶

Take every message down and remove their alarms.

property default: _TagMarkup | None¶

Text markup shown while no message is showing, or None to show nothing.

Raises:

TagMarkupException – the new value is not valid text markup.

property default_attr: dict[Hashable, Hashable] | None¶

Attribute map applied to the default text, or None.

A copy is returned.

Raises:

AttrMapError – a key or value of the new map is not hashable.

dismiss(notification: Notification) → bool¶

Take a message down and remove its alarm.

Returns:

whether the message was showing. It is False for a message that expired or was dismissed before.

property loop: MainLoop | None¶

Loop the alarms are set on, or None to use the loop running at each notify().

property max_count: int | None¶

Messages shown at once, or None for no limit.

A new message over the count dismisses the oldest one. Lowering it dismisses the oldest messages over the new count at once.

Raises:

  • TypeError – the new value is not an int or None.

  • ValueError – the new value is < 1.

property notifications: tuple[Notification, ...]¶

The messages showing, the oldest first.

notify(markup: _TagMarkup, *, severity: Severity = Severity.INFO, timeout: float | Literal[_Unset.UNSET] | None = <unset>) → Notification¶

Show a message below the others.

A call that raises leaves the widget as it was, unless a "change" handler raised. An exception from a handler reaches the caller after the message is showing and its alarm is set.

Parameters:

  • markup – text markup of the message.

  • severity – how serious the message is, which selects its severity_attr entry.

  • timeout – seconds until the message is dismissed, None to keep it until dismiss(), or left out to use timeout.

Returns:

the message, to pass to dismiss().

Raises:

  • TypeError – severity is not a Severity, or timeout is not a number or None.

  • ValueError – timeout is not finite and > 0.

  • TagMarkupException – markup is not valid text markup.

  • RuntimeError – the message has a timeout, there is no loop, and no loop is running. Pass loop= to post a message before the loop runs.

property severity_attr: dict[Severity, dict[Hashable, Hashable]]¶

Attribute map applied to a message for each Severity.

It is set from a mapping of Severity to what AttrMap takes as its attribute map, or None. A severity with no entry is not coloured. A copy is returned.

Raises:

  • TypeError – a key of the new mapping is not a Severity.

  • AttrMapError – a key or value of an attribute map is not hashable.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return flow sizing, whatever is showing.

property timeout: float | None¶

Seconds a message stays when notify() is not given a timeout, or None to keep it.

A new value applies to later messages only.

Raises:

  • TypeError – the new value is not a number or None.

  • ValueError – the new value is not finite and > 0.

WidgetDisable¶

class urwid.WidgetDisable(original_widget: WrappedWidget, *, disabled: bool = True)¶

Decoration widget that disables interaction with the widget it wraps.

While disabled is True, this widget is never selectable, reports no cursor, and always passes focus=False to the wrapped widget, even if it somehow does become the focus. While it is False, focus, input and the cursor pass through to the wrapped widget unchanged. The look of a disabled widget is left to the application, for example an AttrMap around it.

Parameters:

  • original_widget – the widget being disabled

  • disabled – start disabled; False starts with the wrapped widget enabled

>>> from urwid import Button
>>> w = WidgetDisable(Button("Ok"))
>>> w.selectable()
False
>>> w.disabled = False
>>> w.selectable()
True

Wrap original_widget, disabled unless disabled is False.

Whether interaction with the wrapped widget is disabled; setting it redraws the widget.

WidgetPlaceholder¶

class urwid.WidgetPlaceholder(original_widget: WrappedWidget)¶

Do-nothing decoration widget that can be used for swapping between widgets.

Swaps happen without modifying the container of this widget.

This can be useful for making an interface with a number of distinct pages or for showing and hiding menu or status bars.

The widget displayed is stored as the self.original_widget property and can be changed by assigning a new widget to it.

Wrap original_widget, warning when it does not implement the Widget API.

Container Widget Classes¶

Frame¶

class urwid.Frame(body: BodyWidget, header: HeaderWidget | None = None, footer: FooterWidget | None = None, focus_part: Literal['header', 'footer', 'body'] | AbstractWidget = 'body', *, select_navigation: bool = False, flow: bool = False, min_body_rows: int = 0, trim_first: Literal['header', 'footer'] = 'header')¶

Frame widget is a box widget with optional header and footer flow widgets placed above and below it.

It also accepts a flow size, when its body does: the header, the body and the footer then take all their rows. It reports FLOW sizing only with flow set, so containers lay it out as a box widget by default.

Note

The main difference between a Frame and a Pile widget defined as: Pile([(‘pack’, header), body, (‘pack’, footer)]) is that the Frame will not automatically change focus up and down in response to keystrokes.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_part changed, also when removing the header or the footer in focus moves the focus to the body. Its handlers receive the frame, the old and the new focus part.

Initialize a new Frame instance.

Parameters:

  • body – a box widget for the body of the frame, and a flow widget as well for a flow size

  • header – a flow widget for above the body (or None)

  • footer – a flow widget for below the body (or None)

  • focus_part – ‘header’, ‘footer’ or ‘body’

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

  • flow – report FLOW sizing as well when the body reports it, see flow.

  • min_body_rows – rows the body keeps on a short screen, see frame_top_bottom().

  • trim_first – 'header' or 'footer', the part trimmed first while the body is in focus, see frame_top_bottom().

Raises:

  • TypeError – min_body_rows is not an integer.

  • ValueError – focus_part is not one of the three frame parts. min_body_rows is negative. trim_first is not 'header' or 'footer'.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Passing a header, body or footer that does not implement the Widget API is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

property body: BodyWidget¶

Return the body widget.

property contents: MutableMapping[Literal['header', 'footer', 'body'], tuple[BodyWidget | HeaderWidget | FooterWidget, None]]¶

Return a dict-like object similar to the following.

{
    "body": (body_widget, None),
    "header": (header_widget, None),  # if frame has a header
    "footer": (footer_widget, None),  # if frame has a footer
}

This object may be used to read or update the contents of the Frame.

The values are similar to the list-like .contents objects used in other containers with (Widget, options) tuples, but are constrained to keys for each of the three usual parts of a Frame. When other keys are used a KeyError will be raised.

Currently, all options are None, but using the options() method to create the options value is recommended for forwards compatibility.

flow¶

Whether this Frame reports FLOW sizing as well, when its body reports it; see sizing().

property focus: BodyWidget | HeaderWidget | FooterWidget¶

Return the child Widget in focus: the body, header or footer widget. Read-only.

property focus_part: Literal['header', 'footer', 'body']¶

Return which part of the frame is in focus.

Setting it to another part redraws the frame and sends "focus changed". Unlike the focus_position setter, it does not check that the frame has that part.

property focus_position: Literal['header', 'footer', 'body']¶

Return which part of the frame is in focus: ‘body’, ‘header’ or ‘footer’.

Returns:

one of ‘header’, ‘footer’ or ‘body’.

property footer: FooterWidget | None¶

Return the footer widget, or None if there is no footer.

frame_top_bottom(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool) → tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]¶

Calculate the number of rows for the header and footer.

The parts take rows in this order, each one at most the rows it reports, and the body also takes the rest:

  • header in focus: the header, min_body_rows of the body, the footer;

  • footer in focus: the footer, min_body_rows of the body, the header;

  • body in focus: min_body_rows of the body but at least 1, the part trim_first does not name, the part it names.

With the default min_body_rows=0 and trim_first='header', the part in focus is shown first, and with the body or the footer in focus the header is trimmed before the footer.

>>> from urwid import Edit, ListBox, Pile, Text
>>> frame = Frame(ListBox([Text("entry")]), header=Edit("path: "), footer=Pile([Text("flag")] * 3))
>>> frame.frame_top_bottom((10, 4), True)
((0, 3), (1, 3))
>>> frame.min_body_rows = 2
>>> frame.trim_first = "footer"
>>> frame.frame_top_bottom((10, 4), True)
((1, 1), (1, 3))
Parameters:

  • size – See Widget.render() for details

  • focus – True if this widget is in focus

Returns:

(head rows, foot rows),(orig head, orig foot) orig head/foot are from rows() calls.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return the cursor coordinates of the focus widget.

property header: HeaderWidget | None¶

Return the header widget, or None if there is no header.

keypress(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], key: str) → str | None¶

Pass keypress to widget in focus.

With select_navigation, unhandled 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands may cause a focus change.

min_body_rows¶

Rows the body takes in a box size right after the part in focus; see frame_top_bottom().

mouse_event(size: tuple[int, int] | tuple[int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Pass mouse event to appropriate part of frame. Focus may be changed on button 1 press.

options() → None¶

There are currently no options for Frame contents.

Return None as a placeholder for future options.

Render the Frame and return the resulting canvas.

At a flow size every part is rendered in full.

Raises:

Return the total rows of the header, the body and the footer at the width in size.

It is used for a flow size, which shows every part in full. The body has to accept a flow size.

>>> from urwid import ListBox, Text
>>> Frame(ListBox([Text("one"), Text("two")]), header=Text("head"), footer=Text("foot")).rows((10,))

ListBox¶

class urwid.ListBox(body: ListWalker[_K, AbstractFlowWidget], *, select_navigation: bool = False, unfocused_focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr_func: _UnfocusedFocusAttrFunc | None = None, focus_when_empty: bool = True, edge: Literal['return', 'stop'] = 'return', wheel: Literal['focus', 'view'] = 'focus', flow: bool = False)¶
class urwid.ListBox(body: Iterable[AbstractFlowWidget], *, select_navigation: bool = False, unfocused_focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr_func: _UnfocusedFocusAttrFunc | None = None, focus_when_empty: bool = True, edge: Literal['return', 'stop'] = 'return', wheel: Literal['focus', 'view'] = 'focus', flow: bool = False)

Vertically stacked list of widgets.

Create the ListBox widget.

Parameters:

  • body – a ListWalker subclass such as SimpleFocusListWalker that contains widgets to be displayed inside the list box

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

  • unfocused_focus_attr – attribute map applied to the focus child while the list box renders without focus, in any form AttrMap takes; see unfocused_focus_attr.

  • unfocused_focus_attr_func – function that gives the map applied to the focus child while the list box renders without focus, instead of unfocused_focus_attr; see unfocused_focus_attr_func.

  • focus_when_empty – whether the ListBox accepts the input focus while its body is empty; False lets a container move the focus past an empty ListBox.

  • edge – what up at the first row and down at the last row do; see edge.

  • wheel – what a notch of the vertical mouse wheel moves; see wheel.

  • flow – report FLOW sizing as well, so that a container can lay the ListBox out with the rows of all its widgets; see sizing().

Deprecated since version 4.0.2: Passing a body that is not a ListWalker but has a get_focus method is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

property body: ListWalker[_K, AbstractFlowWidget]¶

A ListWalker subclass such as SimpleFocusListWalker that contains widgets.

The widgets are to be displayed inside the list box.

Deprecated since version 4.0.2: Assigning a body that is not a ListWalker but has a get_focus method is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

calculate_visible(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → VisibleInfo | tuple[None, None, None]¶

Return the widgets that would be displayed in the ListBox given the current size and focus.

see Widget.render() for parameter details

Returns:

(middle, top, bottom) or (None, None, None)

middle

(row offset*(when +ve) or *inset*(when -ve), *focus widget, focus position, focus rows, cursor coords or None)

top

(# lines to trim off top, list of (widget, position, rows) tuples above focus in order from bottom to top)

bottom

(# lines to trim off bottom, list of (widget, position, rows) tuples below focus in order from top to bottom)

change_focus(size: tuple[int, int], position: _K, offset_inset: int = 0, coming_from: Literal['above', 'below'] | None = None, cursor_coords: tuple[int | str, int] | tuple[int | str] | None = None, snap_rows: int | None = None) → None¶

Change the current focus widget.

This is used internally by methods that know the widget’s size.

See also set_focus().

Parameters:

  • size – see Widget.render() for details

  • position – a position compatible with self._body.set_focus()

  • offset_inset – either the number of rows between the top of the listbox and the start of the focus widget (+ve value) or the number of lines of the focus widget hidden off the top edge of the listbox (-ve value) or 0 if the top edge of the focus widget is aligned with the top edge of the listbox (default if unspecified)

  • coming_from – either ‘above’, ‘below’ or unspecified None

  • cursor_coords – (x, y) tuple indicating the desired column and row for the cursor, a (x,) tuple indicating only the column for the cursor, or unspecified

  • snap_rows – the maximum number of extra rows to scroll when trying to “snap” a selectable focus into the view

Raises:

  • TypeError – the body does not implement set_focus.

  • ListBoxError – offset_inset leaves no row of the target visible, or cursor_coords names a row outside the target widget.

  • ValueError – the cursor row is unspecified and coming_from is neither 'above' nor 'below'.

property contents: ListBoxContentsProto[_K]¶

An object that allows reading widgets from the ListBox’s list walker.

Widgets are read as a (widget, options) tuple. None is currently the only value for options.

Warning

This object may not be used to set or iterate over contents.

You must use the list walker stored as body to perform manipulation and iteration, if supported.

property edge: Literal['return', 'stop']¶

What up at the first row and down at the last row do.

  • "return": the key is returned unhandled, so a parent container such as Pile moves the focus out of the list.

  • "stop": the key is consumed and the focus stays in the list.

An empty list box returns the key in both modes, since it has no row to keep the focus on.

ends_visible(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → list[Literal['top', 'bottom']]¶

Return a list that may contain 'top' and/or 'bottom'.

i.e. this function will return one of: [], ['top'], ['bottom'] or ['top', 'bottom'].

convenience function for checking whether the top and bottom of the list are visible

flow¶

Whether this ListBox reports FLOW sizing as well, when the body allows it; see sizing().

property focus: AbstractFlowWidget | None¶

The child widget in focus or None when ListBox is empty.

Return the widget in focus according to our list walker.

focus_next_match(predicate: Callable[[AbstractFlowWidget], bool], *, reverse: bool = False, wrap: bool = True) → _K | None¶

Move the focus to the next widget for which predicate returns true.

The body is walked lazily from the position next to the focus in the search direction, so a match before the end of the body is found without reading the rest of it. A wrapped search reads the other side of the focus whole, and checks the widget in focus last, so a single match is found again.

>>> import urwid
>>> listbox = urwid.ListBox([urwid.Text(word) for word in ("apple", "pear", "plum", "peach")])
>>> listbox.focus_next_match(lambda widget: widget.text.startswith("p"))
1
>>> listbox.focus_next_match(lambda widget: widget.text.startswith("p"), reverse=True)
3
>>> listbox.focus_next_match(lambda widget: widget.text == "apple", wrap=False) is None
True
>>> listbox.focus_position
3
Parameters:

  • predicate – called with each candidate widget.

  • reverse – search towards the top of the body.

  • wrap – continue from the other end of the body once this end is reached. Only a body that ends, or declares wrap_around, has an end to stop at; one that cycles without declaring it is searched once round from the focus either way.

Returns:

the new focus position, or None when nothing matches and the focus stays where it was.

IndexError – the ListBox is empty.

get_scrollpos(size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → int¶

get_visible_amount(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the number of items currently visible.

keypress(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Move selection through the list elements scrolling when necessary.

Keystrokes are first passed to widget in focus in case that widget can handle them. A list box with no rows shows nothing and returns every key unhandled.

Keystrokes handled by this widget are:

up

up one line (or widget)

down

down one line (or widget)

page up

move cursor up one listbox length (or widget)

page down

move cursor down one listbox length (or widget)

With edge "stop", up at the first row and down at the last row are consumed.

With select_navigation, unhandled 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands move the focus to the next or previous selectable widget.

make_cursor_visible(size: tuple[int, int]) → None¶

Shift the focus widget so that its cursor is visible.

mouse_event(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], event: str, button: int, col: int, row: int, focus: bool) → bool | None¶

Pass the event to the contained widgets.

May change focus on button 1 press. A vertical wheel notch the widget under the pointer does not handle moves what wheel selects.

Deprecated since version 2.4.0: Support for a contained widget that does not implement mouse_event is deprecated. Support will be removed in version 7.0.

options() → None¶

There are currently no options for ListBox contents.

Return None as a placeholder for future options.

render(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → CompositeCanvas | SolidCanvas¶

Render ListBox and return canvas.

see Widget.render() for details

A flow size renders every widget of the body, with the rows rows() reports.

Raises:

ListBoxError – the rendered contents do not fit the reported rows, a child widget renders a different number of rows or cursor coordinates than it calculated, or the list walker returns a next position pointing at itself.

require_relative_scroll(size: tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → bool¶

Widget require relative scroll due to performance limitations of real lines count calculation.

rows(size: tuple[int], focus: bool = False) → int¶

Return the rows of all widgets in the body at the width in size.

The focus widget is measured in focus and the others out of focus, as a render measures them, whatever focus is. A child whose row count depends on its focus breaks the box layout as well, which a render reports as a ListBoxError.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> ListBox([Text("one two"), Text("three")]).rows((5,))
3
Raises:

ListBoxError – the body does not support the scrolling protocol, or it wraps around.

rows_max(size: tuple[int, int] | None = None, focus: bool = False) → int¶

Scrollable protocol for sized iterable and not wrapped around contents.

scroll_to_bottom() → None¶

Move the focus to the last position of the body and show it at the bottom, as end does.

The last position gets the focus whether its widget is selectable or not, unlike focus_last_selectable(). An empty body is left as it is.

Raises:

TypeError – the body does not implement positions.

scroll_to_top() → None¶

Move the focus to the first position of the body and show it at the top, as home does.

The first position gets the focus whether its widget is selectable or not, unlike focus_first_selectable(). An empty body is left as it is.

Raises:

TypeError – the body does not implement positions.

selectable() → bool¶

Return whether the ListBox accepts the input focus.

With focus_when_empty False it does not while its body is empty.

set_focus(position: _K, coming_from: Literal['above', 'below'] | None = None) → None¶

Set the focus position and try to keep the old focus in view.

Without coming_from, preserve the target widget’s cursor and nested focus. With coming_from, move its cursor from the indicated edge.

Parameters:

  • position – a position compatible with self._body.set_focus()

  • coming_from – set to ‘above’ or ‘below’ if you know that old position is above or below the new position.

Raises:

  • ListBoxError – coming_from is not 'above', 'below' or None.

  • TypeError – the body does not implement set_focus.

  • IndexError – the ListBox is empty.

set_focus_valign(valign: Literal['top', 'middle', 'bottom'] | VAlign | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int]) → None¶

Set the focus widget’s display offset and inset.

Parameters:

valign – one of: ‘top’, ‘middle’, ‘bottom’ (‘relative’, percentage 0=top 100=bottom)

set_scrollpos(position: SupportsInt) → None¶

Scroll the view so that row position of the body is its first row.

The view keeps the size of the last render, and position is limited to the rows that keep it filled. The focus stays where it is while at least one of its rows is in the new view. Otherwise it moves to the selectable widget in the view nearest to the edge the old focus left by:

  • the top edge, when the view moved down past the old focus;

  • the bottom edge, when the view moved up past it.

When the view holds no selectable widget, the widget at that edge takes the focus, as with the cursor keys.

When the focus widget shows a cursor, a render in focus still moves the view to keep the cursor visible.

>>> from urwid import Text
>>> listbox = ListBox([Text(str(number)) for number in range(10)])
>>> canvas = listbox.render((5, 3))
>>> listbox.set_scrollpos(4)
>>> listbox.get_scrollpos(), listbox.focus_position
(4, 4)
>>> listbox.set_scrollpos(3)
>>> listbox.get_scrollpos(), listbox.focus_position
(3, 4)
Raises:

ListBoxError – the body does not support the scrolling protocol, or it wraps around.

shift_focus(size: tuple[int, int], offset_inset: int) → None¶

Move the location of the current focus relative to the top.

This is used internally by methods that know the widget’s size.

See also set_focus_valign().

Parameters:

  • size – see Widget.render() for details

  • offset_inset – either the number of rows between the top of the listbox and the start of the focus widget (+ve value) or the number of lines of the focus widget hidden off the top edge of the listbox (-ve value) or 0 if the top edge of the focus widget is aligned with the top edge of the listbox.

Raises:

ListBoxError – offset_inset falls outside the listbox rows or the rows of the focus widget.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Return BOX, and FLOW as well when flow is set and the body allows it.

The body allows it when it reports its length, or an estimate of it, and does not wrap around. The whole body is measured on each flow layout, so this is meant for lists short enough for a dialog.

update_pref_col_from_focus(size: tuple[int, int]) → None¶

Update self.pref_col from the focus widget.

property wheel: Literal['focus', 'view']¶

What a notch of the vertical mouse wheel moves.

It applies when the widget under the pointer does not handle the notch.

  • "focus": the focus moves one row up or down, as up and down do.

  • "view": the view scrolls one row, and the focus moves as set_scrollpos() moves it. When the cursor of the selectable widget the focus would move to keeps the view from moving one row, the widget at the edge takes the focus instead. When the cursor of the focus widget keeps the view from moving, the notch moves the focus as in "focus".

At the ends of the list the event is returned unhandled in both modes.

Columns¶

class urwid.Columns(widget_list: Iterable[AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget | tuple[Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK], AbstractFlowWidget | AbstractFixedWidget] | tuple[int, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget] | tuple[Literal['given', WHSettings.GIVEN], int, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget] | tuple[Literal['weight', WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget]], dividechars: int = 0, focus_column: int | AbstractWidget | None = None, min_width: int = 1, box_columns: Iterable[int] | None = None, *, select_navigation: bool = False, unfocused_focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr_func: _UnfocusedFocusAttrFunc | None = None)¶

Widgets arranged horizontally in columns from left to right.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of contents. Its handlers receive the container, the old and the new focus position, which is None while it is empty.

Initialize a new Columns instance.

Parameters:

  • widget_list – iterable of flow or box widgets

  • dividechars – number of blank characters between columns

  • focus_column – index into widget_list of column in focus or focused widget instance, if None the first selectable widget will be chosen, skipping columns of width 0, and of weight 0 when min_width is 0, unless no other column is selectable.

  • min_width – minimum width for each column which is not calling widget.pack() in widget_list.

  • box_columns – a list of column indexes containing box widgets whose height is set to the maximum of the rows required by columns not listed in box_columns.

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

  • unfocused_focus_attr – attribute map applied to the focus child while the columns renders without focus, in any form AttrMap takes; see unfocused_focus_attr.

  • unfocused_focus_attr_func – function that gives the map applied to the focus child while the columns renders without focus, instead of unfocused_focus_attr; see unfocused_focus_attr_func.

Raises:

  • ColumnsError – an item of widget_list is not a widget or a valid (width, widget) pair.

  • ValueError – focus_column is a widget that is not in widget_list.

Warns ColumnsWarning:

an item of widget_list is not a widget. A 'pack' column is listed in box_columns.

widget_list may also contain tuples such as:

(given_width, widget)

make this column given_width screen columns wide, where given_width is an int

('given', given_width, widget)

the same as (given_width, widget), in the expanded form that repeats the contents options. 'fixed' is accepted as an older name for 'given'.

('pack', widget)

call pack() to calculate the width of this column

('weight', weight, widget)

give this column a relative weight (number) to calculate its width from th screen columns remaining

Widgets not in a tuple are the same as ('weight', 1, widget)

If the Columns widget is treated as a box widget then all children are treated as box widgets, and box_columns is ignored.

If the Columns widget is treated as a flow widget then the rows are calculated as the largest rows() returned from all columns except the ones listed in box_columns. The box widgets in box_columns will be displayed with this calculated number of rows, filling the full height.

column_widths(size: tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], focus: bool = False) → list[int]¶

Return a list of column widths.

A width of 0 hides the corresponding column completely, and keyboard navigation skips it. A subclass may override this method to lay the columns out itself; every sized layout uses its result.

keypress(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int], key: str) → str | None¶

Pass keypress to the focus column.

A hidden focus column, one with a width of 0, gets no keys: the key is left unhandled by it. Unhandled left and right keys may cause a focus change. The focus moves only to columns the last layout drew, since a column the user cannot see takes no input: a column left 0 wide or not laid out for lack of room is skipped until a resize shows it. With select_navigation, so do unhandled 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands.

Parameters:

  • size – Widget size correct for the supported sizing

  • key – a single keystroke value

Returns:

None if the key was handled, otherwise the key left unhandled, as the focus column returned it.

Raises:

ColumnsError – size is () and the children cannot be sized as a fixed widget.

static options(width_type: Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK], width_amount: int | float | None = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.PACK], None, bool]¶
static options(width_type: Literal['given', WHSettings.GIVEN], width_amount: int = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int, bool]
static options(width_type: Literal['weight', WHSettings.WEIGHT] = WHSettings.WEIGHT, width_amount: int | float = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, bool]
static options(width_type: Literal['pack', 'given', 'weight', WHSettings.PACK, WHSettings.GIVEN, WHSettings.WEIGHT] = WHSettings.WEIGHT, width_amount: int | float | None = 1, box_widget: bool = False) → tuple[Literal[WHSettings.PACK], None, bool] | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int, bool] | tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, bool]

Return a new options tuple for use in a Columns .contents list.

This sets an entry’s width type: one of the following:

'pack'

Call the widget’s Widget.pack() method to determine how wide this column should be. width_amount is ignored.

'given'

Make column exactly width_amount screen-columns wide.

'weight'

Allocate the remaining space to this column by using width_amount as a weight value.

Parameters:

  • width_type – 'pack', 'given' or 'weight'

  • width_amount – None for 'pack', a number of screen columns for 'given' or a weight value (number) for 'weight'

  • box_widget – set to True if this widget is to be treated as a box widget when the Columns widget itself is treated as a flow widget.

Raises:

ColumnsError – width_type and width_amount are not a valid combination.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Sizing supported by widget.

Returns:

Calculated widget sizing

Warns ColumnsWarning:

a column’s width type does not suit its widget’s sizing, or no sizing fits all columns and the BOX/FLOW fallback is used.

Due to the nature of container with mutable contents, this method cannot be cached.

Rules: * WEIGHT BOX -> BOX * GIVEN BOX -> Can be included in FIXED and FLOW depends on the other columns * PACK BOX -> Unsupported * BOX-only widget without box_columns disallow FLOW render

  • WEIGHT FLOW -> FLOW

  • GIVEN FLOW -> FIXED (known width and widget knows its height) + FLOW (historic)

  • PACK FLOW -> FLOW (widget fit in provided size)

  • WEIGHT FIXED -> Need also FLOW or/and BOX to properly render due to width calculation

  • GIVEN FIXED -> Unsupported

  • PACK FIXED -> FIXED (widget knows its size)

Backward compatibility rules: * GIVEN BOX -> Allow BOX

BOX can be only if ALL widgets support BOX. FIXED can be only if no BOX without “box_columns” flag and no strict FLOW.

>>> from urwid import BigText, Edit, SolidFill, Text, Thin3x3Font
>>> font = Thin3x3Font()

# BOX-only widget >>> Columns((SolidFill(“#”),)) <Columns box widget (1 item)>

# BOX-only widget with “get height from max” >>> Columns((SolidFill(“#”),), box_columns=(0,)) <Columns box widget (1 item)>

# FLOW-only >>> Columns((Edit(),)) <Columns selectable flow widget (1 item)>

# FLOW allowed by “box_columns” >>> Columns((Edit(), SolidFill(“#”)), box_columns=(1,)) <Columns selectable flow widget (2 items) focus_column=0>

# FLOW/FIXED >>> Columns((Text(“T”),)) <Columns fixed/flow widget (1 item)>

# GIVEN BOX only -> BOX only >>> Columns(((5, SolidFill(“#”)),), box_columns=(0,)) <Columns box widget (1 item)>

# No FLOW - BOX only >>> Columns(((5, SolidFill(“#”)), SolidFill(“*”)), box_columns=(0, 1)) <Columns box widget (2 items) focus_column=0>

# FIXED only -> FIXED (and FLOW via drop/expand) >>> Columns(((WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“1”, font)),)) <Columns fixed/flow widget (1 item)>

# Invalid sizing combination -> use fallback settings (and produce warning) >>> Columns(((WHSettings.PACK, SolidFill(“#”)),)) <Columns box/flow widget (1 item)>

# Special case: empty columns widget sizing is impossible to calculate >>> Columns(()) <Columns box/flow widget ()>

Pile¶

class urwid.Pile(widget_list: Iterable[AbstractWidget | tuple[Literal['pack', WHSettings.PACK], AbstractFlowWidget | AbstractFixedWidget] | tuple[int, AbstractBoxWidget] | tuple[Literal['given', WHSettings.GIVEN], int, AbstractBoxWidget] | tuple[Literal['weight', WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float, AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget]], focus_item: AbstractWidget | int | None = None, *, select_navigation: bool = False, unfocused_focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr_func: _UnfocusedFocusAttrFunc | None = None)¶

A pile of widgets stacked vertically from top to bottom.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of contents. Its handlers receive the container, the old and the new focus position, which is None while it is empty.

Build the pile from a list of child widgets.

Parameters:

  • widget_list – child widgets

  • focus_item – child widget that gets the focus initially. Chooses the first selectable widget if unset, skipping rows of height or weight 0 unless no other row is selectable.

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

  • unfocused_focus_attr – attribute map applied to the focus child while the pile renders without focus, in any form AttrMap takes; see unfocused_focus_attr.

  • unfocused_focus_attr_func – function that gives the map applied to the focus child while the pile renders without focus, instead of unfocused_focus_attr; see unfocused_focus_attr_func.

Raises:

PileError – an item of widget_list is not a widget or a valid (height, widget) pair.

Warns PileWarning:

an item of widget_list is not a widget.

widget_list may also contain tuples such as:

(given_height, widget)

always treat widget as a box widget and give it given_height rows, where given_height is an int

('given', given_height, widget)

the same as (given_height, widget), in the expanded form that repeats the contents options. 'fixed' is accepted as an older name for 'given'.

('pack', widget)

allow widget to calculate its own height by calling its rows() method, i.e. treat it as a flow widget.

('weight', weight, widget)

if the pile is treated as a box widget then treat widget as a box widget with a height based on its relative weight value, otherwise treat the same as ('pack', widget).

Widgets not in a tuple are the same as ('weight', 1, widget)`

Note

If the Pile is treated as a box widget there must be at least one 'weight' tuple in widget_list.

property contents: MonitoredFocusList[tuple[AbstractFlowWidget | AbstractFixedWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.PACK], None]] | tuple[AbstractBoxWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int]] | tuple[AbstractBoxWidget | AbstractFlowWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.WEIGHT], int | float]]]¶

The contents of this Pile as a list of (widget, options) tuples.

options currently may be one of

('pack', None)

allow widget to calculate its own height by calling its rows method, i.e. treat it as a flow widget.

('given', n)

Always treat widget as a box widget with a given height of n rows.

('weight', w)

If the Pile itself is treated as a box widget then the value w will be used as a relative weight for assigning rows to this box widget. If the Pile is being treated as a flow widget then this is the same as ('pack', None) and the w value is ignored.

If the Pile itself is treated as a box widget then at least one widget must have a ('weight', w) options value, or the Pile will not be able to grow to fill the required number of rows.

This list may be modified like a normal list and the Pile widget will updated automatically.

See also

Create new options tuples with the options() method

The child widget in focus or None when Pile is empty.

sizing() → frozenset[Sizing]¶

Sizing supported by widget.

Returns:

Calculated widget sizing

Warns PileWarning:

an item’s height type does not suit its widget’s sizing.

Due to the nature of container with mutable contents, this method cannot be cached.

Rules: * WEIGHT BOX -> BOX * GIVEN BOX -> FLOW (height is known) & BOX (can be shrinked/padded) * PACK BOX -> Unsupported

  • WEIGHT FLOW -> FLOW

  • GIVEN FLOW -> Unsupported

  • PACK FLOW -> FLOW

  • WEIGHT FIXED -> Need also FLOW or/and BOX to properly render due to width calculation

  • GIVEN FIXED -> Unsupported

  • PACK FIXED -> FIXED (widget knows its size)

>>> from urwid import BigText, ProgressBar, SolidFill, Text, Thin3x3Font
>>> font = Thin3x3Font()

# BOX-only widget >>> Pile((SolidFill(“#”),)) <Pile box widget (1 item)>

# GIVEN BOX -> BOX/FLOW >>> Pile(((10, SolidFill(“#”)),)) <Pile box/flow widget (1 item)>

# FLOW-only >>> Pile((ProgressBar(None, None),)) <Pile flow widget (1 item)>

# FIXED -> FIXED >>> Pile(((WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“0”, font)),)) <Pile fixed widget (1 item)>

# FLOW/FIXED -> FLOW/FIXED >>> Pile(((WHSettings.PACK, Text(“text”)),)) <Pile fixed/flow widget (1 item)>

# FLOW + FIXED widgets -> FLOW/FIXED >>> Pile((ProgressBar(None, None), (WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“0”, font)))) <Pile fixed/flow widget (2 items) focus_item=0>

# GIVEN BOX + FIXED widgets -> BOX/FLOW/FIXED (GIVEN BOX allows overriding its height & allows any width) >>> Pile(((10, SolidFill(“#”)), (WHSettings.PACK, BigText(“0”, font)))) <Pile widget (2 items) focus_item=0>

# Invalid sizing combination -> use fallback settings (and produce warning) >>> Pile(((WHSettings.WEIGHT, 1, BigText(“0”, font)),)) <Pile box/flow widget (1 item)>

# Special case: empty pile widget sizing is impossible to calculate >>> Pile(()) <Pile box/flow widget ()>

GridFlow¶

class urwid.GridFlow(cells: Iterable[AbstractFlowWidget], cell_width: int, h_sep: int, v_sep: int, align: Literal['left', 'center', 'right'] | Align | tuple[Literal['relative', WHSettings.RELATIVE], int], focus: int | AbstractFlowWidget | None = None, *, select_navigation: bool = False, unfocused_focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr_func: _UnfocusedFocusAttrFunc | None = None)¶

Flow widget that renders all the widgets it contains the same width.

Arranges them from left to right and top to bottom.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of contents. Its handlers receive the container, the old and the new focus position, which is None while it is empty.

Create the GridFlow widget.

Parameters:

  • cells – iterable of flow widgets to display

  • cell_width – column width for each cell

  • h_sep – blank columns between each cell horizontally

  • v_sep – blank rows between cells vertically (if more than one row is required to display all the cells)

  • align – horizontal alignment of cells, one of: ‘left’, ‘center’, ‘right’, (‘relative’, percentage 0=left 100=right)

  • focus – widget index or widget instance to focus on

  • select_navigation – handle the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands over the cells in their contents order, see Moving the Focus with Tab.

  • unfocused_focus_attr – attribute map applied to the focus child while the grid renders without focus, in any form AttrMap takes; see unfocused_focus_attr.

  • unfocused_focus_attr_func – function that gives the map applied to the focus child while the grid renders without focus, instead of unfocused_focus_attr; see unfocused_focus_attr_func.

align¶

Alignment of each row of cells.

property base_widget: GridFlow¶

Return self: GridFlow is a container, not a decoration.

property cell_width: int¶

The width of each cell in the GridFlow.

Setting this value affects all cells.

property contents: MonitoredFocusList[tuple[AbstractFlowWidget, tuple[Literal[WHSettings.GIVEN], int]]]¶

The contents of this GridFlow as a list of (widget, options) tuples.

options is currently a tuple in the form (‘given’, number). number is the number of screen columns to allocate to this cell. ‘given’ is the only type accepted at this time.

This list may be modified like a normal list and the GridFlow widget will update automatically.

See also

Table¶

class urwid.Table(columns: Sequence[TableColumn], rows: Iterable[Sequence[_Cell] | TableRow] = (), *, header: bool = True, header_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, footer: Sequence[_Cell] | None = None, footer_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, header_drop: int | None = None, footer_drop: int | None = None, dividechars: int = 1, attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr: _AttrMapLike | None = None, unfocused_focus_attr_func: Callable[[TableRow], _AttrMapLike | None] | None = None, max_rows: int | None = None, row_attr: Callable[[int, Any], _AttrMapLike | None] | None = None, select_navigation: bool = False, wheel: Literal['focus', 'view'] = 'focus', scrollbar: bool | None = False, **scrollbar_options: Unpack[_ScrollBarOptions])¶

Rows of cells in columns of shared widths, between a fixed header and footer, and with a focused row.

The rows scroll in a ListBox. The header stays on top, the footer stays at the bottom, and neither takes the focus. It is a box and flow widget, and a fixed widget as well when no column is weighted.

A box size that does not fit the whole table drops the header or the footer by header_drop and footer_drop. A part with a threshold is dropped while keeping it leaves the body fewer rows than the threshold. The part with the larger threshold is dropped first; on equal thresholds the footer goes first. A part that is kept but does not fit is cut at the bottom. The header keeps its rows first, so the footer is cut first.

Sends "focus changed" after focus_position changed, also through a change of body, with the old and the new position, which is None while the table is empty. A row replaced in place at the focus sends nothing. Sends "activate" with the focus position when the focused row leaves the activate command (enter and space by default) unhandled. A handler whose result is true consumes the key; otherwise the key is returned, as Overlay does for "menu". Every handler runs, whatever the earlier ones returned. A mouse click moves the focus and reaches the cell only.

Create the table.

Parameters:

  • columns – one specification per column; their number is the number of cells of every row

  • rows – the initial rows, as TableRow objects of layout or sequences of cells

  • header – draw the column labels above the rows

  • header_attr – attribute map of the header

  • footer – the cells of a row drawn below the rows, see footer; None draws no footer

  • footer_attr – attribute map of a footer built from cells

  • header_drop – in a box size whose rows do not all fit, drop the header while keeping it leaves the body fewer rows than this; None never drops it

  • footer_drop – the same threshold for the footer

  • dividechars – blank screen columns between two visible columns

  • attr – attribute map of a row without its own TableRow.attr

  • focus_attr – attribute map of the focused row without its own TableRow.focus_attr

  • unfocused_focus_attr – attribute map applied to the focused row while the table renders without focus, over the row’s own map, as ListBox.unfocused_focus_attr does

  • unfocused_focus_attr_func – function that gives that map for the focused row, instead of unfocused_focus_attr; see unfocused_focus_attr_func

  • max_rows – the most rows of body a flow size shows; None shows every row

  • row_attr – row_attr(index, data) called each time a row renders, see row_attr

  • select_navigation – let the 'next selectable' and 'prev selectable' commands (tab and shift tab) move across the cells and then to the next or previous row

  • wheel – what a notch of the mouse wheel moves; see wheel

  • scrollbar – True draws a scrollbar beside the rows, None only when the rows do not fit, False never; while it is on, its column counts in the natural width

  • scrollbar_options – the ScrollBar parameters with a scrollbar_ prefix, such as scrollbar_thumb_char, scrollbar_end_markers, scrollbar_side and scrollbar_attr; ignored while scrollbar is False

Raises:

  • TableError – a column specification, dividechars, max_rows, a drop threshold, a row or the footer is invalid.

  • TypeError – a keyword argument is neither a parameter of the table nor one of scrollbar_options, also while scrollbar is False.

  • ValueError – ScrollBar rejects the value of a scrollbar_ parameter.

property body: _TableRows¶

The rows of the table, below the header.

A sequence of cells added to it becomes a TableRow of layout, so body[i] is that row. A change is validated before it is applied, and a TableError leaves the rows unchanged. Replace every row with table.body[:] = rows.

property focus: TableRow | None¶

The row in focus, or None when the table is empty.

property focus_position: int¶

The index of the row in focus.

Raises:

IndexError – the table is empty, or the position set is not an index of a row.

property footer: TableRow | None¶

The row below the rows, such as totals or a summary, or None.

It shares the column widths, and its cells count in the PACK widths. Set it to a sequence of cells, which becomes a row mapped by footer_attr alone, to a TableRow of layout, which keeps its own maps and may be a span row, or to None. A text cell of the footer re-measures its column when its text changes, as in any row.

Raises:

TableError – a row is of another layout or is in body, or the cells do not fit the columns.

get_cursor_coords(size: tuple[()] | tuple[int] | tuple[int, int]) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Return the cursor coordinates of the focused row, below the header.
